newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia joins Bank for International Settlements.
newsitem.headline: Croatia joins Bank for International Settlements.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Monday it had been formally accepted as a member of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) at the annual meeting in Basle, Switzerland.

Two others of the six former Yugoslav republics -- Slovenia and Macedonia -- gained full membership of the BIS, while Bosnia's acceptance was delayed over "organisational and staffing issues," a statement from Croatia's national bank said.

The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, was not invited to join as it refused to cooperate in the division of the former Yugoslavian central bank's stake in the international institution.

BIS was founded in 1930 when it united European central banks to deal with war reparations. Its annual meeting is attended by central bankers from all over the world. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
